rationale:
Selected major: 1.1.0 -> 2.0.0.

Assessed the complete candidate from v1.1.0 (012f572) through develop 0104e44ad71657814e37c4219fbb18158e6f4de6, including PRs #7, #9, #10 and #11. The provider changes remove a supported HTTP contract and change processing authority, so the highest impact is major. The documented pre-production exception applied only to v1.0.0 -> v1.1.0 and is not reused.

- HTTP (breaking): POST /v1/memory-processing/consent is replaced by POST /v1/memory-processing/provider with scope/system inputs. Capabilities replace consents and consentVersion with options. Shared consent schemas/types are removed. Provider selection and PROCESSING_PROVIDER_SELECTED audit events are added; consolidation result metadata gains optional exclusion/deferred counts and typed explanations. Evidence: packages/shared/src/{memory-processing,enums}.ts, apps/api/src/memory-processing/memory-processing.controller.ts and docs/openapi.json.
- MCP: supported tool names, input/output schemas, aliases and transports remain unchanged from 1.1.0. The processing routes above use browser-session authentication and are not MCP tool endpoints. The existing app permission and shared memory-request/suggestion contracts used by packages/mcp/src/tools.ts remain unchanged. Existing MCP integrations need no schema adaptation for this release.
- Identity/OAuth: accounts, sessions, client credentials, OAuth grants, scopes, refresh rotation and revocation remain compatible. The new migration adds an owner-linked preference table and an audit enum value; it does not rewrite identity or grant records. Evidence: packages/db/prisma/migrations/20260924010000_processing_provider_preference/migration.sql and unchanged auth/OAuth contracts. Active voice sessions should reconnect because new sessions use an extraction-only configuration fingerprint.
- Authority (breaking): a per-owner provider choice authorizes each processing task without separate TypeSafe consent. Explicit legacy revocations migrate to OpenAI; active or absent consent rows inherit the instance default. The selector has no off state, so a prior revocation that stopped extraction can now allow OpenAI processing. Unset task defaults prefer TypeSafe when its required credentials exist. TypeSafe extraction still sends normalization work to OpenAI. App disclosure permissions, owner isolation, secret checks and consolidation review/automatic settings remain separate. Each provider stage and commit rechecks the current choice; switching blocks stale work. Evidence: docs/adr/0046-owner-selected-memory-processing-providers.md, memory-processing-config.service.ts, processing-permission.service.ts, extraction-provider.service.ts, consolidation-writer.service.ts, memory-processing.e2e.spec.ts and tenant-isolation.e2e.spec.ts.
- Data: existing vault data and historical consent/audit records are retained. The additive migration creates ProcessingProviderPreference with owner/scope uniqueness, value constraints and cascading ownership, and maps revoked TypeSafe consents to system_2. Export/import remains funes-vault.export.v2; exports add optional processing.providerPreferences. Import still restores its documented memory/client/policy subset rather than processing history or preferences. Evidence: packages/shared/src/data-control.ts, apps/api/src/data-control/{vault-export,vault-import}.service.ts and the migration SQL. Back up the database, stop old processing services, migrate, then start matching images. Rollback requires the pre-upgrade database and 1.1.0 images; no real vault reset.
- Deployment: Node 24, pinned pnpm, image/service names, origins and environment variable names remain compatible. MEMORY_EXTRACTION_SYSTEM and MEMORY_CONSOLIDATION_SYSTEM now set initial owner defaults; absent selectors prefer configured TypeSafe as described above, so operators must review defaults before rollout. Deploy matching API/worker, web and MCP images and reconnect voice. Existing jobs retain provider snapshots; explicit reprocessing can adopt the current choice. Evidence: docs/memory-processing.md, memory-processing-config.service.ts, voice-sessions.service.ts, and unchanged Dockerfile/Compose/environment contracts. Publication and deployment are separate from preparing these PRs.

Compatible fixes also persist the consolidation toggle immediately with rollback on save failure, report expected privacy exclusions as successful consolidation rather than incomplete work, distinguish true failure/deferred reasons, and synchronize voice tool feedback with source persistence and extraction. Evidence: PRs #7, #9 and #10 and their component, unit, integration and browser tests.
